glance.text: Two ADAU1860s wired on one clock (the demo's one-codec-per-ear layout); board B failed at its codec, with ADI support. 1797 board mapped and its Pi 4 ready.
1860 loop delay 94.5 µs at 48 kHz, 12.8 µs at 192 kHz; DVNC ceiling 2.5–3.5 dBA at the ear; S(z) on Mon 2 Nov.
HS01 node: LED rings running on Wi-Fi; HR + IMU next. Headband-to-cup mount printed.
Did not move: DSMA STALL rule, AERO-A storage (disk 93 % full) and GPS gate, wired headset route, Huey radio into DEV-A, DEV-B power.
0 of 5 met (the bench went to the two-1860 rig and the 1797 board).
VGSA film v10; F03 social posts round 1; RV-8 x-ray engine reel.
Quiet since 23 Oct: no comment, chat or card move from anyone (read 30 Oct). Five of your cards close today.

last_week.reading: Not met. No server change since 22 Oct (BRAVO's write-up: package updates and off-box backups still open).

rows.title: WS4 — PPG proof-out in the foam earcup at the mastoid
rows.note: No PPG work this week. The headset node that will carry the SparkFun heart-rate sensor is wired and its first stage (the LED rings) runs; the HR sensor is stage 2, next week. Nothing new from Stefan's lane (KILO) in the team repo.

rows.title: Confirm ADAU1860-1 can drive H1 transducers, or specify an external amp
rows.note: A donor-headset driver played cleanly from the 1860 (26 Oct); not yet measured into 150/300/600 Ω. John measured the 1860's analog loop on our rig board: 94.5 µs at 48 kHz, 12.8 µs at 192 kHz (7.4× less), polarity inverted by the codec; unity gain and 0.012 % THD in the 1 Oct recordings. Mon 2 Nov John drives the cup's own driver from the 1860 (M8). Peter owns the amp call.

rows.title: Evaluate IMU's
rows.note: Closing: done last week on F02 + F03 (ICM-45686 = the production DVNC reference, John 21 Oct). John added the timing this week: vibration leads sound by at most ~1.4 ms on the one pair with no clock uncertainty, and the DEV-A/DEV-B capture clocks differ by 51.6 ppm (~90 ms per 30 min), so the next rig runs every codec on one clock.

rows.title: Evaluate Microphones
rows.note: Closing: done last week (cabin mic = analogue IM68A130A, no I2S mic; John 21 Oct). This week John measured DVNC's ceiling at the pilot's ear on F03: 2.5–3.5 dBA over 20 Hz–1 kHz on both aircraft, ~85 % of in-band energy tonal, and proposes DVNC's band as 20 Hz–1 kHz, the same as ANC. The next step needs a mic inside the cup.

rows.title: Run X-Plane + ArduPilot SITL campaign — characterise where the ArduPilot math falls short
rows.note: No SITL campaign work this week (the rig only made the VGSA 'Headphones on' lab reel). Still to settle on the rig before 1 Dec: one DSMA STALL rule (the fix is 8/8 on real stalls but adds 27 false STALLs on 62 rig stalls).

rows.title: WS3 — Build the demo H1: donor internals in printed shells, passthrough audio proven
rows.note: Two pieces toward the demo headset: a printed mount that joins a donor headband's metal tab to our ear cup (designed 26 Oct, PLA), and headset node HS01 on a XIAO ESP32-C6: both 16-LED rings run from a control page it serves over the office Wi-Fi (27 Oct); the heart-rate sensor and IMU, streaming to AERO-A, are next. A donor driver played from the 1860. Passthrough audio not started.

rows.title: AeroNode auto-detects record start/stop and auto-pushes to AeroSync
rows.note: No work this week: start/stop is still manual. The DEV-A recorder fixes (STARTs refused while grading) carry to before 1 Dec.

rows.title: Bench-test relay-driven headset comms (relays + oscilloscope)
rows.note: No bench readings this week: the bench went to the two-1860 rig and the 1797 board. The procedure and record sheets (pinout, PTT contacts, ohms per earcup, A20 pigtail) are ready.

rows.title: Initial data model for the AeroNode synchronous timeline
rows.note: Done, closing. The model puts every IMU, both Pixhawks and DEV-A/DEV-B audio on one timeline (sync pulse + start/stop/mark) and held one clock on all four F03 flights (2.4–4.7 µs rms). This week: John measured what separate codec clocks cost (51.6 ppm) and the next rig runs both ears' codecs on one clock master. Peter's written review can go on the card once his access is set up.

rows.title: Source a calibrated SPL meter
rows.note: Closing: done last week (RS PRO DT-8852, Class 2, flew all four F03 flights; evidence in the W43 summary). Follow-up still open: check it against a 94 dB / 1 kHz calibrator.

rows.title: Test AeroVault crash capture with the CM5-to-memory link severed
rows.note: No work this week: the 10-minute test procedure is written and waits for a bench day.

rows.title: Test DSMA SAFE/CAUTION cues in a real flight and log the cue output
rows.note: Closing: done last week. F03 flight 2 (16 Oct): DSMA live in the pilot's headset, every cue logged; CAUTION 15/10/5 and the beep before both stalls. STALL is a separate problem (rule fault, fix not yet proven on the rig) and stays open under 'Validate DSMA in real-world flight'.

rows.title: Test the PureVoice concept using microphone and CM5
rows.note: No work this week. Last week's commitment (re-run on the recorded ear mic P11 for both RV-8 flights and Huey 2) was not met and carries.

rows.title: Validate DSMA in real-world flight on development hardware
rows.note: No work this week. Open for 1 Dec: the STALL rule (8/8 real stalls in replay, 27 false on 62 rig stalls), approach callouts, the aircraft weight, and a wired headset route (Bluetooth dropped 3 times on F03).

rows.title: Validate the AeroVault high-G / shock trigger and crash data dump
rows.note: No work this week. Still to do: a bench shock test of the impact trigger (12 g over 20 ms, armed above 30 kt with a GPS fix).

rows.title: WS5 — Measure passive attenuation of the printed cup + cushion on the EARS Pro
rows.note: No attenuation figure yet. John has the cup, driver, mics, miniDSP EARS, RME and an ADAM A7X in the office on Mon 2 Nov for the secondary-path measurements; the printed cup's passive number could be taken on the same set-up.

rows.title: Build the acoustic bench and measure baseline noise cancelling
rows.note: Bench rig for the demo's one-codec-per-ear audio: two ADAU1860s wired on DEV-A on one clock (27 Oct). Board B then failed at its codec (clock pins open at U15, no I²C on two hosts); support case open with ADI, board A works. ADAU1797 eval board mapped from 80 microscope photos; a new Pi 4 drives it over SPI (build sheet, firmware, 11-step guide). John's M0–M12 run sheet and loop delay on our board; S(z) on Mon 2 Nov.

other_hours.label: Company videos: VGSA investor film v7–v10, F03 social posts, RV-8 engine reel; fleet admin and this report.
other_hours.detail: VGSA investor demo film v7 → v10 with BRAVO's 3-D sound stage (Mon, ~5 h). F03 social posts: 21 ideas with 37 numbers checked, HOTEL's first four reels, DELTA's 'Headphones on' reel (Wed–Thu, ~4 h). RV-8 x-ray engine reel with CHARLIE, BRAVO and ECHO (Wed–Thu, ~5 h). Fleet admin: agent check-ins, INDIA's self-test fix, the W44 page and this report (~3 h).

blockers:
- ADAU1860 board B failed (since 27 Oct): its codec lost its clock pins and stopped answering I²C. Support case open with Analog Devices; the one-codec-per-ear rig waits on a replacement board.
- ADAU1797 eval board has no public schematic (since 21 Oct): mapped from photos instead; its switch and jumper functions are still unknown.
- The 1 Dec fixes did not move this week (all since 16 Oct): the DSMA STALL rule is unproven on the rig; AERO-A storage stalls (its disk is now 93 % full) and the 6X GPS gate; a wired headset route to replace Bluetooth; the Huey radio getting into DEV-A's I2S; DEV-B power, with FOXTROT (its agent) idle since 14 Oct.
- Peter's access to the boxes (SSH key, Tailscale), since 22 Sep.

comments.comment:
30 Oct: closing. Done last week: the cabin mic is the analogue IM68A130A into the ADAU1372, no I2S mic (John, 21 Oct).
This week John measured what DVNC can do at the pilot's ear on F03: 2.5–3.5 dBA over 20 Hz–1 kHz on both aircraft (only 0.5–2.0 dBA over 20–250 Hz), with ~85 % of in-band energy tonal. He proposes DVNC's band as 20 Hz–1 kHz, the same as ANC's.
Next step (on the DVNC cards): the same calculation on a mic inside the cup.
Evidence: reports/john/2026-10-29_dvnc_measured_ceiling_and_band.html (team repo).

30 Oct: closing. Done last week: the RS PRO DT-8852 (Class 2, ±1.4 dB) flew all four F03 flights, live into AERO-A and in its own memory (they agree within 0.24 dB).
Follow-up kept open in the report's needs: check it against a 94 dB / 1 kHz calibrator. Evidence: chris/golf/2026-W43_fleet_week_F03.md.

comments.card: Initial data model for the AeroNode synchronous timeline
comments.comment:
30 Oct (Chris): Done, closing.
- The working model puts every IMU, both Pixhawks and the DEV-A/DEV-B audio on one timeline from a sync pulse and start/stop/mark commands; it held one clock on all four F03 flights (2.4–4.7 µs rms).
- John's analysis places every sample on UTC and corrects the 3.891 s start offset and the 51.6 ppm clock difference between the boxes (reports/john/2026-10-26_imu_audio_timebase.html).
- The next rig runs every codec on one clock master (two-1860 build, 27 Oct).
@Peter your written review is still welcome here once your access (SSH key, Tailscale) is set up.
